blocks.x: Identity lifecycle done properly: joiner-mover-leaver automation that revokes on the leaver SLA, privileged access in vaults instead of spreadsheets, standing admin accounts driven to zero — and MFA that people actually complete.
Identity is the perimeter now — and it runs on process, not enthusiasm

Identity is where most breaches begin and where most programs under-invest: accounts outlive their owners, service accounts share passwords, and privileged access is granted with a ticket and forgotten. Modernization is lifecycle engineering — every identity born with an owner, moved with re-attestation, and killed on schedule.

Machine identity gets the same discipline as humans: workload identities with short-lived credentials, secrets vaulted and rotated, and the hygiene score reported weekly because credential rot is a countdown, not an event.
Below: the failure modes that turn identity programs into audit findings, the reference architecture of the lifecycle, and the console that keeps revocation honest.
Four identity failures auditors find first
Every one of these is a process failure, not a tool failure — the countermeasures bind the lifecycle to HR and operational reality so revocation is an event, not a TODO.

blocks.x: Reference architecture — lifecycle from joiner to leaver

The lifecycle is event-driven: joiners provisioned from HR truth, movers re-scoped by role change, leavers revoked on SLA — and privileged access checked out of vaults just-in-time, reviewed, and never standing.

blocks.note: Elevation is time-bound and recorded: standing admin access is replaced by just-in-time grants whose sessions are recorded and whose grants expire on a clock.

widgets.title: The identity fabric — click nodes for the lifecycle contract

nodes.label: HR system of record
nodes.detail: Joiner-mover-leaver events drive everything: identities born, moved and retired here — the org chart and the access truth converge.

nodes.label: Authoritative directory
nodes.detail: One directory with federated authentication; passkeys/FIDO2 for humans, workload federation for machines — phishing-resistant by default.

nodes.label: Mined RBAC
nodes.detail: Roles mined from the access graph's actual usage patterns — entitlement packs that describe work, not checkbox archaeology.

nodes.label: JIT elevation
nodes.detail: Standing admin replaced by time-boxed, session-recorded elevation with approval routing — privilege is an event, not a state.

nodes.label: Non-human identities
nodes.detail: Service accounts, workload identities and agent identities under the same registry discipline — owners, scopes, rotation, revocation.

nodes.label: Policy enforcement
nodes.detail: Access decisions at resources (zero-trust style) with toxic-combination blocking — the graph's findings become runtime policy.

nodes.label: Access reviews
nodes.detail: Evidence-based reviews: usage data pre-attached, rubber-stamping detectable, decisions fed back into RBAC mining.

widgets.note: Click nodes for the lifecycle contract each layer carries. The review lane feeds the RBAC miner — access governance that learns.
